ITQAN:v1p89#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p89#2/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p89#2/r7.claim: The author replies that Ibn Abbas knew the wording was broader but identified the intended referent, as the Prophet interpreted ظلم as shirk while Companions grasped its general scope.
ITQAN:v1p89#2/r7.anchor: أجيب عن ذلك بأنه لا يخفى عليه أن اللفظ أعم من السبب لكنه بين أن المراد باللفظ خاص

TABATABAI:12:22-34#27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:22-34#27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:22-34#27/r3.claim: Qur’anic assurances that God’s friends have no fear or grief and that the secure are guided describe this state of joy and safety.
TABATABAI:12:22-34#27/r3.anchor: ألا إن أولياء الله لا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون

BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r4.claim: The secure believers are those who do not mix faith with shirk; idolaters wrongly claim idol worship completes their faith as a means of approach and intercession.
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r4.anchor: لم يخلطوه {بظلم} أي : بشرك كما يفعله الفريق المشركون حيث يزعمون أنهم يؤمنون بالله تعالى

BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r5.claim: The idols’ claimed role is refuted by the idolaters’ own claim that they worship them only to bring them nearer to God.
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r5.anchor: ما نعبدهم إلا ليقربونآ إلى الله زلفى

BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#4/r6.claim: Only the believers free of shirk have security from punishment.

BURSEVI:v3p45#5/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p45#5/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p45#5/r1.claim: Those believers are guided to truth, while everyone outside their group is in manifest error.
BURSEVI:v3p45#5/r1.anchor: {وهم مهتدون} إلى الحق ومن عداهم في ضلال مبين.

QASHANI:6:80-86/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:80-86/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:80-86/r3.claim: Faith without injustice means essential monotheism unmingled with self-manifestation or any remnant of self, which is hidden association; its reward is true security and guidance.
QASHANI:6:80-86/r3.anchor: من ظهور نفس القلب أو وجود بقية فإنها شرك خفي

SULAMI:v1p206#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p206#3/r1.speaker: ابن طاهر
SULAMI:v1p206#3/r1.claim: Those who do not mix faith with wrongdoing never turn to anyone besides God in trials; they are secure and return to the One who is their final refuge.
SULAMI:v1p206#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن طاهر : لم يلبسوا إيمانهم أي : لم يرجعوا في النوائب والمهمات إلى غير الله

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p156#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p156#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p156#6/r1.claim: They did not mix faith with shirk; Luqmān calls shirk a great injustice.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p156#6/r1.anchor: إيمانهم بظلم} أي: لم يخلطوه بشرك

NAHHAS:v2p79/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p79/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p79/r3.claim: الذين آمنوا begins a sentence; أولئك begins another, لهم الأمن is its predicate, and the full clause predicates the first; وهم مهتدون is another subject-predicate clause.
NAHHAS:v2p79/r3.anchor: مبتدأ ( أولئك ) ابتداء ثان ( لهم الأمن ) خبره والجملة خبر الأول ( وهم مهتدون ) ابتداء وخبر

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r1.claim: Faith unmixed with wrongdoing means faith not mixed with shirk.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، قوله : الذين امنوا ولم يلبسوا ايمانهم بظلم ، يقول : لم يخلطوا ايمانهم بشرك .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r2.claim: When the Companions feared any sin violated the verse, the Prophet explained that it means shirk, citing Luqman 31:13.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r2.anchor: قالوا : اينا لم يظلم نفسه ؟ فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ليس كما تظنون ، انما قال لقمان لابنه : لا تشر بالله ان الشرك لظلم عظيم .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r3.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r3.claim: An alternative report says the assurance applied specifically to Abraham.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r3.anchor: عن زياد بن حرملة قال : سئل علي ، عن هذه الاية ولم يلبسوا ايمانهم بظلم قال : هذه لابراهيم خاصة .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r4.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r4.claim: The source says this verse was thought to concern a former enemy who embraced Islam, fought, and died after asking whether Islam could benefit him.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1333/r4.anchor: عن بكر بن سوادة قال : حمل رجل من العدو علي المسلمين فقتل رجلا ، ثم حمل فقتل اخر ، ثم حمل فقتل اخر ، ثم قال : اينفعني الاسلام بعد هذا ؟

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، النبي ﷺ
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r1.claim: A destitute Bedouin traveled to learn from the Prophet, accepted Islam, then died accidentally; the Prophet called him one who acted little yet earned much and among the secure and guided.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كنا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسيرة سراة ، اذ عرض له اعرابي فقال : يا رسول الله ، والذين بعثك بالحق

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r2.claim: Being guided means possessing proof through knowledge and uprightness.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r2.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق : اولئك لهم الامن وهم مهتدون ، والهدى في الحجة بالمعرفة والاستقامة .

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ، عبد الله بن سخبرة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r3.claim: Those patient in trials, grateful for gifts, forgiving wrongs, and seeking forgiveness are promised security and guidance.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1334/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن سخبرة رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : من ابتلي فصبر ، واعطي فشكر ، وظلم فغفر وظلم فاستغفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p323/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p323/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p323/r1.claim: Abraham's people acknowledged God while associating other gods with Him, as Arabs did; this fits Quranic arguments about creation and the analogy between Abraham's people and Arab polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p323/r1.anchor: لأن قومه كانوا يعترفون بالله ويشركون معه في الإلهية غيره كما كان إشراك العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r6.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r6.claim: The majority take those who believe as Abraham's continuation answering which party is safer; he answers his own question because the answer is undeniable, thereby silencing his opponents.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r6.anchor: هذه الجملة من حكاية كلام إبراهيم على ما ذهب إليه جمهور المفسرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas compares this to a learned person who asks and answers himself, using the formula if you ask, I say.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p331/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كما يسأل العالم ويجيب نفسه بنفسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r1.claim: Another view treats the clause as God's fresh statement confirming Abraham, not part of his speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r1.anchor: وقيل : ليس ذلك من حكاية كلام إبراهيم ، وقد انتهى قول إبراهيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r2.claim: A third view makes it the people's reply, but the author rejects this: one expects it to say those who believed said so, and they remained obstinate enough to throw Abraham into the fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r2.anchor: ولا يصح لأن الشأن في ذلك أن يقال : قال الذين آمنوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r3.claim: The object of believed is omitted because the context makes it clear: they believe in God.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r4.claim: Labisa literally means mix and metaphorically means combining similar beliefs or actions at once; the phrase likens faith and shirk to mixed substances, as in 2:42.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r4.anchor: يخلطوا ، وهو هنا مجاز في العمل بشيئين متشابهين في وقت واحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r5.claim: Wrongdoing here is associating others with God in belief and worship, the greatest violation of the sole rightful object of worship; the author cites Ibn Masud's sound hadith about the verse and Luqman's statement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود ( لما نزلت { الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r6.speaker: النبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r6.claim: In the sound report from Ibn Masud, Muslims feared the verse meant ordinary self-wrong; the Prophet explains it as shirk, quoting Luqman that association is great wrongdoing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r6.anchor: ليس كما تظنون إنما هو كما قال لقمان لابنه : { إن الشرك لظلم عظيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r7.claim: The mixing metaphor fits because belief in God and shirk are alike in kind as claims about lordship; the meaning is believers who do not worship partners with God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p332/r7.anchor: لأن شأن الأجسام المتماثلة أن يكون اختلاطها أشد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari extends wrongdoing to sins generally, citing 9:36 and reading the verse through the Mu'tazili view that sinners lack assurance against eternal punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r1.anchor: وحمل الزمخشري الظلم على ما يشمل المعاصي ، لأن المعصية ظلم للنفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r2.claim: The author rejects that reading: if Abraham speaks, he had called only to monotheism before receiving a law; if God speaks, the verse supports Abraham's point, so sins do not fit either context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r2.anchor: فالحق أن الآية غير محتاجة للتأويل على أصولهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r3.claim: The demonstrative those signals that people with the preceding description deserve the predicate, as in the verse about those guided by their Lord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r3.anchor: وهذا كقوله { أولئك على هدى من ربهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r4.claim: The lām in for them is a lām of exclusive and established possession, stronger than simply saying they are safe; security covers worldly destruction and afterlife punishment because only monotheism was required then.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r4.anchor: أشارت اللام إلى أن الأمن مختص بهم وثابت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r5.claim: The definite al-amn denotes the same generic security raised in the prior verse, not an anaphoric definite whose repeated reference needs explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p333/r5.anchor: والتعريف في { الأمن } تعريف الجنس ، وهو الأمن المتقدم ذكره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r1.claim: If the pronoun in they are guided is a separator, guidance is restricted to monotheists without shirk, as in the cited Quranic phrasing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r1.anchor: والضمير للفصل ليفيد قصر المسند على المسند إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r2.claim: Alternatively, they are guided is a full nominal sentence and a second report about the relative clause; the pronoun is its subject, not a separator, so it does not imply exclusivity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r2.anchor: فيكون خبرا ثانيا عن اسم الموصول ، ويكون ذكر ضمير الجمع لأجل حسن العطف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r3.claim: This alternative uses a full sentence for smoother coordination with the prior nominal sentence, a device also found in the cited verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p334/r3.anchor: وهذا من محسنات الوصل كما عرف في البلاغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r3.claim: The believers’ ẓulm here means shirk, established by Prophetic and Companion reports; the anxious Companions were told it meant the shirk described by Luqman as great wrongdoing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r3.anchor: و «الظلم» في هذه الآية الشرك تظاهرت بذلك الأحاديث عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r4.claim: ʿUmar asked Ubayy ibn Kaʿb about the verse when he found it troubling; Ubayy explained it as shirk and reassured him. A similar exchange involved Zayd ibn Suhan and Salman.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r4.anchor: وروي أن عمر بن الخطاب قرأ في المصحف فلما أتى عليها عظمت عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r5.claim: Mujahid reads bi-shirk in place of bi-ẓulm; ʿIkrima reads yulbisū with a ḍamma on the yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد، «ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بشرك» وقرأ عكرمة «يلبسوا» بضم الياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r6.claim: Al-amn is a nominative subject whose predicate is prepositional; the clause predicates security of them, and mahditūn means rightly guided.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r6.anchor: والأمن رفع بالابتداء وخبره في المجرور والجملة خبر أولئك، وهم مهتدون أي راشدون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وعكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r7.claim: ʿAli says the believers are Ibrahim in particular; ʿIkrima says they are the Prophet’s emigrant Companions in particular.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r7.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: المراد بهذه الآية إبراهيم خاصة، وقال عكرمة: نزلت في مهاجري أصحاب محمد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj takes the statement as words of Ibrahim’s people, whose acknowledgment of truth itself forms part of the proof despite their wrongdoing; the excerpt ends mid-explanation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p315#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن جريج هي من قول قوم إبراهيم ويجيء هذا من الحجة أيضا أن أقروا بالحق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r1.claim: Not mixing faith with wrongdoing means not mixing it with shirk; an authentic report from Ibn Masʿud says Muslims worried until the Prophet identified the wrongdoing as shirk and cited 31:13.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r1.anchor: أي يخلطوه بشرك روى البخاري ومسلم في صحيحيهما من حديث ابن مسعود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r2.claim: One view, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, says the verse refers to Abraham and his companions, with another report limiting it to Abraham alone, not this community.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r2.anchor: أنه إبراهيم وأصحابه وليست في هذه الأمة قاله علي بن أبي طالب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r3.speaker: عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says it refers to those who migrated to Medina.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r3.anchor: أنه من هاجر إلى المدينة قاله عكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r4.claim: A third view makes the verse general to all believers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r4.anchor: والثالث أنها عامة ذكره بعض المفسرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r5.claim: Exegetes also differ on whether this statement is Abraham’s words to his people or God’s response.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p77#3/r5.anchor: وهل هي من قول إبراهيم لقومه أم جواب من الله تعالى فيه قولان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r2.claim: Those who believe without mixing faith with shirk devote worship to God alone; they are secure on Judgment Day and guided in this life and the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r2.anchor: أي: هؤلاء الذين أخلصوا العبادة لله وحده لا شريك، له، ولم يشركوا به شيئا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r3.claim: When the verse troubled the Companions, the Prophet clarified through Luqman's words that the injustice meant here is shirk, not every sin or wrong against oneself.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p294/r3.anchor: وقالوا: يا رسول الله، فأينا لا يظلم نفسه؟ (5) قال: "إنه ليس الذي تعنون!

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295/r1.claim: Ibn Mardawayh transmits that when the verse was revealed, the Prophet was told: You are among those described by it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: لما نزلت: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم} قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "قيل لي: أنت منهم"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295/r2.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295/r2.claim: Jarir narrates a traveler who accepts the Prophet's basic teachings, dies when his camel falls into a rodent hole, and is described as one with little work but great reward; angels place Paradise's fruit in his mouth because he died hungry, and the Prophet directs that he be buried in a niche.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295/r2.anchor: ثم قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "هذا من الذين قال الله، عز وجل: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r1.claim: A second Jarir route repeats the traveler story and the Prophet's description of the man as having done little yet earned much.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r1.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله، فذكر نحوه، وقال فيه: "هذا ممن عمل قليلا وأجر كثيرا"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports a Bedouin who leaves home, possessions, and family seeking the Prophet's guidance, accepts Islam, and dies in an accidental fall; the Prophet affirms his sincere quest and says he is among those secure and guided without shirk.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس قال: كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسير (2) ساره، إذ عرض له أعرابي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r3.claim: A report from Ibn Umar describes the secure and guided as those who respond to favor with gratitude, deprivation with patience, personal wrongdoing with seeking forgiveness, and injury with pardon.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p295#2/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من أعطي فشكر ومنع فصبر وظلم فاستغفر

JISHUMI:v3p2306/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r1.claim: The reading of ‘We raise’ varies between nun plus genitive annexation, nun with accusative indefinite ‘degrees,’ and Yaʿqub's yāʾ form at the parallel Yusuf passage.
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو: (نرفع) بالنون (درجات من نشاء)

JISHUMI:v3p2306/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r2.claim: Faith means affirmation linguistically; in religious usage it names performing obligations and avoiding major sins. Lubs means mixing; proof is evidence relied on for a claim.
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r2.anchor: الإيمان: هو التصديق في اللغة، وفي الشرع: اسم لأداء الواجبات

JISHUMI:v3p2306/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r3.speaker: ابن زيد وابن إسحاق وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r3.claim: ‘Those who believe’ may be God's own answer, settling the dispute between Abraham and his people by declaring which party is secure.
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r3.anchor: قيل: من الله على جهة فصل القضاء بذلك بين إبراهيم وقومه، عن ابن زيد وابن إسحاق وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v3p2306/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r4.claim: Alternatively, Abraham's people answer his question about which group deserves security, giving evidence against themselves.
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r4.anchor: وقيل: جواب قومه لما سألهم: أي الفريقين أحق بالأمن؟

JISHUMI:v3p2306/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r5.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r5.claim: Another view makes Abraham answer his own question; the author also treats this as continuation of Abraham's argument for unity, justice, promise, and warning.
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو جواب إبراهيم كما يسأل العالم ويجيب نفسه، حكاه الزجاج

JISHUMI:v3p2306/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r6.claim: ‘They did not mix faith with wrongdoing’ means they did not commit shirk, identified as great wrongdoing in 31:13; a prophetic report reassured Companions troubled by the verse.
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r6.anchor: قيل: بشرك، عن ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب وأبي بكر وحذيفة وسلمان

JISHUMI:v3p2306/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r7.claim: Another interpretation includes harm to oneself or others and major sins, not minor sins expiated by obedience or repentance; the garment metaphor also suggests a grave sin affecting deeds.
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r7.anchor: وقيل: أراد ظلم نفسه وظلم غيره، والمراد به الكبائر دون الصغائر

JISHUMI:v3p2306/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r8.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r8.claim: Security is safety from punishment on Judgment Day; guidance means Paradise or truth and religion.
JISHUMI:v3p2306/r8.anchor: أولئك لهم الأمن يعني المستبصر في الدين آمن يوم القيامة من العذاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r6.claim: Believers who do not mix faith with wrongdoing avoid sins that make them impious; interpreting wrongdoing as unbelief conflicts with ‘mix.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p40#3/r6.anchor: أي لم يخلطوا إيمانهم بمعصية تفسقهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r1.claim: The injustice here is associating partners with God; Ibn Masʿūd reports that the verse worried Muslims until the Prophet explained it by citing Luqmān's description of shirk as grave injustice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r1.anchor: في الظلم ها هنا قولان : أحدهما : أنه الشرك , قاله ابن مسعود , وأبي بن كعب

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd relates that the Prophet said the injustice meant shirk, citing Luqmān's statement that shirk is grave injustice.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( ليس كما تظنون , وإنما هو كما قال لقمان لابنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r3.claim: Another view takes injustice as all kinds of wrongdoing, debated as either general or restricted in scope.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r3.anchor: أنه سائر أنواع الظلم . ومن قال بهذا اختلفوا في عمومها وخصوصها

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r4.speaker: علي كرم الله وجهه
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r4.claim: On the restricted reading, this verse applied to Abraham alone and not to this community.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r4.anchor: أن هذه الآية نزلت في إبراهيم خاصة وليس لهذه الأمة منها شيء

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r5.claim: Another restricted reading applies it to those who migrated to Medina.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r5.anchor: أنها فيمن هاجر إلى المدينة , قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد وابن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r6.claim: The statement is God's answer, distinguishing Abraham from the people who disputed with him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r6.anchor: أنه جواب من الله تعالى فصل به بين إبراهيم ومن حاجه من قومه

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r7.claim: It is the people's answer to Abraham's question about which group deserves security, inadvertently proving his case against them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r7.anchor: أنه جواب قومه لما سألهم { أي الفريقين أحق بالأمن

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r8.claim: It is Abraham answering himself, as a learned person may pose and answer a question.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r8.anchor: كما يسأل العالم نفسصه فيجيبها , حكاه الزجاج

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r9.claim: One account of Abraham's proof contrasts powerless idols with the one who controls benefit and harm; the disputants concede the latter is more worthy.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r9.anchor: أتعبدون من دون الله ما لا يملك لكم ضرا ولا نفعا } أم تعبدون من يملك الضر والنفع

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r10.claim: Another account says Abraham asked whether security belongs to worship of one God or many gods, and they admitted it belongs to the one God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r10.anchor: عبادة إله واحد أم آلهة شتى ؟ فقالوا : عبادة إله واحد

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r11.claim: A third account says Abraham answered their threat that idols might harm him by asking whether they feared pairing small and great gods in worship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r11.anchor: فقال : أما تخافون أن تخبلكم آلهتكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r12.claim: The proof may have occurred to Abraham through God's prompting, or God may have directly taught it to him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p137#2/r12.anchor: أن الله تعالى أخطرها بباله حتى استخرجها بفكره . والثاني : أنه أمره بها ولقنه إياها

MUQATIL:6:82-86/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:82-86/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:82-86/r1.claim: The faithful who do not mix belief with shirk are secure and guided; Abraham’s people conceded his argument, and God granted him this proof and raises whom He wills.
MUQATIL:6:82-86/r1.anchor: يعنى ولم خلطوا تصديقهم بشرك، فلم يعبدوا غيره،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#4/r1.speaker: الصديق
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#4/r1.claim: Here ظلم means associating partners with God, according to al-Ṣiddīq; such believers receive security and guidance.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p332#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم ﴾ بشرك عن الصديق رضى الله عنه

SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r1.claim: The clause ‘those who believe’ may be spoken by Abraham, by his people as an answer against themselves, or by God instructing the Prophet; it may also be God’s independent statement.
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { الذين آمنوا }: هل هو من كلام إبراهيم أو من كلام قومه أو من كلام الله تعالى؟ ثلاثة أقوال للعلماء

SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r2.claim: If Abraham or his people answer, or God instructs the Prophet to answer, ‘those who believe’ is predicate to an implied ‘they’; if God simply reports, it is a subject with several possible predicates.
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r2.anchor: فإن قلنا: إنها من كلام إبراهيم جوابا عن السؤال في قوله: " فأي الفريقين " وكذا إن قلنا: إنها من كلام قومه

SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r3.claim: On the independent-report reading, one parse makes ūlāʾika the second subject, al-amn a third subject, and lahum its predicate, with the nested clauses as predicates in sequence.
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r3.anchor: أنه الجملة بعده فإن " أولئك " مبتدأ ثان، و " الأمن " مبتدأ ثالث، و " لهم " خبره،

SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r4.claim: A second parse makes ūlāʾika apposition or explanatory apposition, lahum the predicate of alladhīna, and al-amn the subject governed by the predicate phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r4.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون " أولئك " بدلا أو عطف بيان، و " لهم " خبر الموصول، و " الأمن " فاعل به لاعتماده.

SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r5.claim: A third parse keeps that structure but makes lahum a fronted predicate and al-amn a delayed subject.
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r5.anchor: الثالث: كذلك، إلا أن " لهم " خبر مقدم، و " الأمن " مبتدأ مؤخر، والجملة خبر الموصول.

SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r6.claim: A fourth parse makes ūlāʾika a second subject, lahum its predicate, and al-amn the active subject, with that clause predicating the relative.
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r6.anchor: الرابع: أن يكون " أولئك " مبتدأ ثانيا، و " لهم " خبره و " الأمن " فاعل به، والجملة خبر الموصول.

SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر النحاس والحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r7.claim: Abu Jaʿfar al-Nahhas and al-Hawfi make lahum al-amn the predicate and ūlāʾika a separator; the author calls this odd because demonstratives do not serve as separators.
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r7.anchor: الخامس: وإليه ذهب أبو جعفر النحاس والحوفي أن " لهم الأمن " خبر الموصول، وأن " أولئك " فاصلة وهو غريب،

SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r8.claim: If alladhīna is predicate to an omitted subject, ūlāʾika begins the next clause; an omitted ‘say/they said’ introduces the earlier clause, spoken by Abraham or his people.
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r8.anchor: وأما على قولنا بأن " الذين " خبر مبتدأ محذوف فيكون " أولئك " مبتدأ فقط، وخبره الجملة بعده

SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r9.claim: ‘And they did not mix’ may continue the relative clause or be circumstantial, meaning they believed without mixing faith with wrongdoing; 19:20 is a parallel.
SAMIN-DURR:6:82/r9.anchor: وقوله " ولم يلبسوا " يجوز فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنها معطوفة على الصلة فلا محل لها حينئذ

SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r1.claim: The cited 19:20 shows a negative clause used circumstantially: Mary says no human has touched her.
SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r1.anchor: أنى يكون لي غلام ولم يمسسني بشر

SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r2.claim: The author dismisses Ibn ʿAsfur’s claim that a negative circumstantial clause is rare and Ibn Khuruf’s claim that its wāw is obligatory when it has a resumptive pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r2.anchor: ولا يلتفت إلى قول ابن عصفور حيث جعل وقوع الجملة المنفية حالا قليلا،

SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r3.claim: The majority read yalbisū with fatḥa, ‘they mix’; ʿIkrima reads with ḍamma from form IV, ‘they make mix.’
SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r3.anchor: والجمهور على " يلبسوا " بفتح الياء بمعنى يخلطونه، وقرأ عكرمة بضمها من الإلباس.

SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:82#2/r4.claim: ‘And they are guided’ may be an independent sentence or a circumstantial clause.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وعلي وسلمان وحذيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r4.claim: Abu Bakr, Ali, Salman, and Hudhayfa interpret the wrong that faith must not be mixed with as shirk.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r4.anchor: الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم } أي بشرك قاله أبو بكر الصديق وعلي وسلمان وحذيفة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the words are Abraham's own answer, as when a teacher asks and answers his own question.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هو من قول إبراهيم كما يسأل العالم ويجيب نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r6.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Abraham's people said the words, giving an answer that became evidence against them.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو من قول قوم إبراهيم أي أجابوا بما هو حجة عليهم قاله ابن جريج

QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r7.claim: When the Companions feared that every wrong disqualified them, the Prophet explained the verse by citing Luqman's statement that associating partners with God is grave injustice.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r7.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ليس هو كما تظنون إنما هو كما قال لقمان لابنه

QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:81-82/r8.claim: Being guided refers to guidance in this worldly life.

RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r4.claim: Abraham’s answer defines full security through faith and freedom from wrongdoing, representing perfected theoretical and practical capacities.
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r4.anchor: أولهما : الإيمان وهو كمال القوة النظرية . وثانيهما : { ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم } وهو كمال القوة العملية

RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r5.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī’s theological school argues that faith remains compatible with major sin: if avoiding all wrongdoing were already part of faith, adding it as a separate condition would be pointless.
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r5.anchor: لو كان ترك الظلم أحد أجزاء مسمى الإيمان لكان هذا التقييد عبثا

RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r6.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that security requires both faith and absence of wrongdoing, so the sinner cannot have security and is subject to the threat of punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v13p49#2/r6.anchor: فوجب أن لا يحصل الأمن للفاسق وذلك يوجب حصول الوعيد له

STUDYQURAN:6:74/r56.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r56.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r56.claim: The wrongdoing that obscures belief is specifically shirk, or idolatry.
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r56.anchor: those who do not obscure their belief in God through shirk, or idolatry (IK, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:6:74/r57.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r57.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r57.claim: Some understand the secure believers as those who combine faith with good works of every kind.
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r57.anchor: For some, this refers to those who combine their faith with good works of all kinds (R)

STUDYQURAN:6:74/r58.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r58.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r58.claim: When Companions feared that no one could avoid all wrongdoing, the Prophet clarified that wrongdoing here means idolatry.
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r58.anchor: The Prophet responded by indicating that what is meantby wrongdoing here is precisely idolatry

STUDYQURAN:6:74/r59.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r59.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r59.claim: The Prophet says the secure and guided are thankful in ease, patient in deprivation, seek forgiveness after wrongdoing, and forgive those who wrong them.
STUDYQURAN:6:74/r59.anchor: thankful when they receive, who are patient when they are denied, who seek forgiveness when they have done wrong

TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r1.claim: God gives the decisive ruling between Abraham and his idolatrous opponents: those who sincerely worship and affirm God without associating anything with Him are safer from His punishment.
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r1.anchor: هذا فصل القضاء من الله بين إبراهيم خليله عليه السلام وبين من حاجه من قومه من أهل الشرك بالله

TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r2.claim: Here ظلم means shirk; idolaters fear God’s punishment both in worldly life and the painful punishment of the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r2.anchor: ولم يخلطوا عبادتهم إياه، وتصديقهم له، بظلم، يعني: بشرك، ولم يشركوا في عبادته شيئا

TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the ظلم as shirk, while adding that no one is entirely free of sins.
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن إن كنتم تعلمون} [الأنعام: 81] قال: فقال الله وقضى بينهم: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم}

TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r4.claim: A second reported interpretation makes the verse Abraham’s people’s answer: believers who worship God alone without mixing faith with shirk deserve security.
TAB-FULL:v9p367#2/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: هذا جواب من قوم إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم لإبراهيم حين قال لهم: أي الفريقين أحق بالأمن؟

TAB-FULL:v9p369/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p369/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v9p369/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports that Abraham’s people answer that worshippers of one Lord, without idolatry, are the secure and guided party; he calls this Abraham’s argument.
TAB-FULL:v9p369/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج: {فأي الفريقين أحق بالأمن إن كنتم تعلمون} [الأنعام: 81] أمن يعبد ربا واحدا أم من يعبد أربابا كثيرة؟

TAB-FULL:v9p369/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p369/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p369/r2.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that God, rather than Abraham’s people, declares who is secure: otherwise the idolaters would have conceded the monotheism they opposed.
TAB-FULL:v9p369/r2.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك عندي بالصواب، قول من قال: هذا خبر من الله تعالى عن أولى الفريقين بالأمن،

TAB-FULL:v9p369/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p369/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v9p369/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the companions worried that ordinary wrongdoing excluded them from security; the Prophet explains that the ظلم here is shirk, citing Luqman.
TAB-FULL:v9p369/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: لما نزلت هذه الآية: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا} [الأنعام: 82] إيمانهم بظلم شق ذلك على أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v9p371/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r1.claim: In Ibn Masud’s report, the Prophet reassures those troubled by the verse that its ظلم means associating partners with God, as Luqman says.
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r1.anchor: قال: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ليس كما تظنون، وإنما هو كما قال لقمان لابنه: لا تشرك بالله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم "

TAB-FULL:v9p371/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r2.speaker: علقمة
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r2.claim: Alqama glosses the ظلم that faith must not be mixed with as shirk.
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r2.anchor: عن الأعمش، عن إبراهيم، عن علقمة، في قوله: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم} [الأنعام: 82] قال: «بشرك»

TAB-FULL:v9p371/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r3.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi likewise glosses the ظلم as shirk.
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r3.anchor: عن منصور، عن إبراهيم، في قوله: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم} [الأنعام: 82] قال: «بشرك»

TAB-FULL:v9p371/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r4.speaker: أبو بكر
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r4.claim: Abu Bakr is reported to interpret the ظلم as shirk.
TAB-FULL:v9p371/r4.anchor: عن أبي بكر: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا} [الأنعام: 82] إيمانهم بظلم قال: «بشرك»

TAB-FULL:v9p374/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r1.speaker: سلمان
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r1.claim: Salman tells Zayd ibn Suhan that the ظلم in the verse is shirk; Zayd says he is glad to have heard the explanation.
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r1.anchor: فقال سلمان: «هو الشرك بالله تعالى» فقال زيد: ما يسرني بها أني لم أسمعها منك

TAB-FULL:v9p374/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r2.speaker: حذيفة
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r2.claim: Hudhayfa is reported to gloss the verse’s ظلم as shirk.
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r2.anchor: عن حذيفة، في قوله: {ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم} [الأنعام: 82] قال: «بشرك»

TAB-FULL:v9p374/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported with both glosses shirk and kufr; he also connects shirk with Luqman’s description of it as grave ظلم.
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم} [الأنعام: 82] يقول: " لم يلبسوا إيمانهم بالشرك، وقال: {إن الشرك لظلم عظيم} [لقمان: 13]

TAB-FULL:v9p374/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r4.claim: When Umar worries that everyone commits ظلم, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb explains that the verse means faith unmixed with shirk.
TAB-FULL:v9p374/r4.anchor: قال: " غفر الله لك، أما سمعت الله تعالى يقول: {إن الشرك لظلم عظيم} [لقمان: 13] ؟ إنما هو: ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بشرك

TAB-FULL:v9p375/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p375/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v9p375/r1.claim: Ubayy reassures Umar that the verse’s ظلم is shirk, invoking the description of shirk as grave injustice.
TAB-FULL:v9p375/r1.anchor: فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين، إن هذا ليس بذاك، يقول الله تعالى: {إن الشرك لظلم عظيم} [لقمان: 13] ، إنما ذلك الشرك "

TAB-FULL:v9p375/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p375/r2.speaker: أبو ميسرة
TAB-FULL:v9p375/r2.claim: Abu Maysara interprets the ظلم as shirk.
TAB-FULL:v9p375/r2.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، عن أبي ميسرة، في قوله: {ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم} [الأنعام: 82] قال: «بشرك»

TAB-FULL:v9p377/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p377/r1.speaker: قتادة، السدي، ابن إسحاق، مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v9p377/r1.claim: Qatada, al-Suddi, Ibn Ishaq, and other early authorities interpret the ظلم as shirk; Mujahid specifies worship of idols, and a report from Ibn Masud connects this explanation to the Prophet’s answer to the companions.
TAB-FULL:v9p377/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم} [الأنعام: 82] ، «أي بشرك»

TAB-FULL:v9p377/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p377/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p377/r2.claim: Another view takes ظلم generally as any forbidden act or neglected command, implying only the sinless are assured security; its proponents answer that the verse addresses a particular group, with sinners who avoid shirk left to God’s will.
TAB-FULL:v9p377/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: ولم يخلطوا إيمانهم بشيء من معاني الظلم. وذلك فعل ما نهى الله عن فعله، أو ترك ما أمر الله بفعله،

TAB-FULL:v9p377/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p377/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p377/r3.claim: The general reading is limited by its proponents to a special group: Ibrahim, according to some, or the Emigrants, according to others; other sinners who avoid shirk remain subject to divine pardon or punishment.
TAB-FULL:v9p377/r3.anchor: فإن شاء لم يؤمنه من عذابه، وإن شاء تفضل عليه فعفا عنه.

TAB-FULL:v9p378/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p378/r1.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v9p378/r1.claim: Ali says this assurance was specific to Abraham and does not apply to this community.
TAB-FULL:v9p378/r1.anchor: عن علي، قال: «هذه الآية لإبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصة، ليس لهذه الأمة منها شيء»

TAB-FULL:v9p378/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p378/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v9p378/r2.claim: Ikrima says the verse specifically concerns those who migrated to Medina.
TAB-FULL:v9p378/r2.anchor: عن قيس بن الربيع، عن سماك، عن عكرمة: {الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم} [الأنعام: 82] قال: «هي لمن هاجر إلى المدينة»

TAB-FULL:v9p378/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p378/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p378/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the sound report from Ibn Masud and the Prophet: the ظلم in this passage is shirk.
TAB-FULL:v9p378/r3.anchor: وأولى القولين بالصحة في ذلك، ما صح به الخبر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم،

ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r3.claim: The statement ‘they have security’ may be God’s own words rather than Abraham’s quoted speech; either attribution is possible.
ZAJJAJ:v2p269/r3.anchor:
قالوا جائز أن يكون هذا قول الله (أولئك لهم الأمن) غير حكاية عن
إبراهيم، وجائز أن يكون إبراهيم قال ذلك.

TABATABAI:6:82/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82/r1.claim: Several linked nominal clauses strongly assert that safety and guidance belong to believers who have not covered their faith with wrongdoing.
TABATABAI:6:82/r1.anchor: تأكيدا قويا من جهة اسنادات متعددة في جمل اسمية

TABATABAI:6:82/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82/r2.claim: Covering is a metaphor: wrongdoing does not erase innate faith, but conceals it and blocks its proper beneficial effect.
TABATABAI:6:82/r2.anchor: فهو استعارة قصد فيها الإشارة إالى أن هذا الظلم لا يبطل أصل الإيمان

TABATABAI:6:82/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82/r3.claim: Although wrongdoing is general in form, the context narrows it to the kind that harms faith and suppresses its good effects.
TABATABAI:6:82/r3.anchor: المراد بالظلم هو نوع الظلم الذي يؤثر أثرا سيئا في الإيمان

TABATABAI:6:82/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82/r4.claim: People broadened wrongdoing from unjustly violating social rights to violating laws, committing sins, disobeying God, and even unintentionally damaging their own health.
TABATABAI:6:82/r4.anchor: توسعوا بعد ذلك فسموا كل مخالفة لقانون أو سنة جارية ظلما

TABATABAI:6:82#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r1.claim: Not every kind of wrongdoing harms faith: mistakes from forgetfulness, ignorance, or lack of awareness do not obstruct faith's path to true felicity.
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r1.anchor: ما كل فرد من أفراده بمؤثر أثرا سيئا في الإيمان

TABATABAI:6:82#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r2.claim: The verse conditions faith's protection from the misery of sins on avoiding wrongdoing that corrupts faith's effect.
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r2.anchor: اشتراط الإيمان في إعطائه الأمن من كل ذنب ومعصية يفسد أثره

TABATABAI:6:82#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r3.claim: Voluntary wrongdoing varies with understanding: at the threshold of monotheism, shirk is the wrong that blocks faith's safety.
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r3.anchor: فالظلم اللائح لهذا الإنسان هو الشرك بالله والإيمان بغيره بالربوبية

TABATABAI:6:82#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r4.claim: After monotheism, major sins such as disobeying parents, consuming an orphan's property, murder, adultery, and drinking wine are the relevant wrongdoing; avoiding major sins brings forgiveness for lesser ones.
TABATABAI:6:82#2/r4.anchor: وعده الله أن يكفر عنه السيئات والمعاصي الصغيرة إن اجتنب كبائر

TABATABAI:6:82#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82#3/r1.claim: At higher spiritual levels, wrongdoing includes disfavored acts, neglecting recommended acts, indulging in permissible things, moral failings, and whatever obstructs love and nearness to God.
TABATABAI:6:82#3/r1.anchor: كإتيان المكروهات وترك المستحبات والتوغل في المباحات

TABATABAI:6:82#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82#3/r2.claim: Faith secures each person only when free of wrongdoing appropriate to that spiritual rank; in this debate the wrong is shirk and the safety is from eternal punishment, while the verse independently has broader force.
TABATABAI:6:82#3/r2.anchor: فالإيمان في كل من هذه المراتب إنما يؤمن المتلبس به ويدفع عنه الشقاء

TABATABAI:6:82#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r1.claim: Faith here first means belief in lordship; excluding wrongdoing specifies belief in Allah's true lordship and rejection of partners, distinguishing warranted faith from unsupported partner worship.
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r1.anchor: المراد بالإيمان هو الإيمان بالربوبية دون الإيمان بوجود صانع العالم

TABATABAI:6:82#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r2.claim: The verse's universal application concerns every sin that harms faith, safety from its misery, and release from its misguidance, though its immediate debate concerns shirk.
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r2.anchor: وكذا المراد بالأمن مطلق الأمن من شقاء المعاصي والذنوب

TABATABAI:6:82#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r3.claim: A commentator reads wrongdoing universally to include harm to oneself or others, in religious or worldly life, and takes security to cover both religious punishment and worldly consequences.
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r3.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين في معنى عموم الظلم في الآية

TABATABAI:6:82#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r4.claim: The commentator says God may forgive many worldly wrongs through mercy and may punish or forgive in the afterlife for sins short of shirk.
TABATABAI:6:82#4/r4.anchor: وإن كان الله تعالى لسعة رحمته لا يعاقب كل ظالم على كل ظلم

TABATABAI:6:82#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r1.claim: The commentator says absolute safety from divine punishment is unavailable to accountable people except for the reverential awe of the spiritually complete.
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r1.anchor: أن الأمن المطلق من الخوف من عقاب الله الديني والدنيوي أو الشرعي والقدري جميعا لا يصح لأحد من المكلفين

TABATABAI:6:82#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r2.claim: If the wrongdoing means major shirk, the commentator says believers are safe from eternal punishment while remaining between fear and hope for lesser sins.
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r2.anchor: وأما معنى الآية على فرض عدم الإطلاق فهو أن الذين آمنوا ولم يخلطوا إيمانهم

TABATABAI:6:82#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r3.claim: He also claims the verse is universal and cites the Companions' understanding as evidence.
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r3.anchor: قال وظاهر الآية هو العموم واستدل عليه بفهم الصحابة

TABATABAI:6:82#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r4.claim: Tabatabai rejects the commentator's reading: the Companions understood wrongdoing as sin, whereas his universal definition includes non-sinful acts.
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r4.anchor: ما استدل عليه من العموم بفهم الصحابة هو غير ما قرره من معنى العموم

TABATABAI:6:82#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r5.claim: The verse describes faith's effects when not covered by wrongdoing; it does not describe every effect of wrongdoing, such as accidental damage to bodily health.
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r5.anchor: وأما ما لا يعد معصية كأكل الغذاء المضر بصحة البدن خطاء

TABATABAI:6:82#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r6.claim: If no accountable person can meet the commentator's absolute condition, his reading leaves the verse with no real instance and no argumentative benefit.
TABATABAI:6:82#5/r6.anchor: ولازمه سقوط الكلام عن الفائدة، وأي فائدة في أن يوضع في الحجة

TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r2.claim: When the verse troubled people who thought everyone sins, the Prophet explained that the intended wrongdoing was shirk, as Luqman calls it great wrongdoing.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال لما نزلت هذه الآية

TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r3.claim: Tabatabai identifies the “righteous servant” in the report as Luqman and infers that al-An'am was revealed after Luqman; shirk is the contextual application and cannot be forgiven like other sins.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r3.anchor: المراد بالعبد الصالح لقمان على ما حكاه الله تعالى من قوله

TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r4.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r4.claim: A report says a traveler accepted Islam after asking the Prophet about faith, then died in an accident; the Prophet counted him among those with faith and no wrongdoing and said he had earned much reward with little action.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r4.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله قال خرجنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r5.speaker: رسول الله
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r5.claim: In the same report, the Prophet says he saw the deceased receiving fruit from the houris, and the narrator explains that the man had died hungry.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#32/r5.anchor: هذا من الذين عملوا قليلا وأجروا كثيرا

TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r1.claim: Tabatabai notes similar versions from Ibn Abbas and the Prophet, and a report in which a man asks about the verse before a new Muslim fights and is martyred.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r1.anchor: ورواه أيضا عن الحكيم الترمذي وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن عباس نحوه

TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r2.claim: A report attributed to Ali says the verse was revealed specifically about Abraham and his companions, not this Muslim community.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب في قوله

TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r3.claim: Tabatabai rejects restricting the verse to Abraham's community because faith and wrongdoing affect innate human nature across all peoples and eras.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r3.anchor: الآية لا تشتمل بمضمونها على حكم خاص تختص به أمة دون أمة

TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r4.claim: A commentator speculates that Abraham's community needed only monotheism because Hammurabi's code supplied civil and ethical law, while Muslims were accountable to a complete revealed law.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r4.anchor: لعل مراده أن الله خص إبراهيم وقومه بأمن موحدهم من عذاب الآخرة

TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r5.claim: Tabatabai rejects the Hammurabi explanation: its chronology does not fit Abraham's era, and the king's own inscriptions invoke numerous pagan gods.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#33/r5.anchor: حمورابي هذا كان يعيش على رأس سنة ألف وسبع مائة قبل المسيح

TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r1.claim: The Torah's legal material cannot establish that Mosaic law adopted Hammurabi: the Torah was lost in Babylonian captivity, later reconstructed by Ezra amid Babylonian legal customs, and nonrevealed laws may still contain sound rulings.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r1.anchor: كيف يحكم بأن الله أمضى في الشريعة الكليمية كثيرا من شرائع حمورابي

TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r2.claim: Abu Basir reports from Imam al-Sadiq that the injustice mixed with faith means associationism; another transmission from Abu Basir says it means doubt.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r2.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم } قال هو الشرك

TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r3.claim: Al-Ayyashi transmits Abu Basir's report from Imam al-Sadiq identifying the people who mixed faith with injustice as the Kharijites and their followers.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r3.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سألت عن قول الله الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم

TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r4.claim: Yaqub ibn Shuayb reports from Imam al-Sadiq that the injustice is misguidance and what exceeds it.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r4.anchor: وفيه عن يعقوب بن شعيب عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم

TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r5.claim: The reports variously identify injustice as associationism, doubt, Kharijite belief, misguidance, or loyalty to the enemies of the Imams; this variety supports a general term with degrees suited to different levels of understanding.
TABATABAI:6:74-83#35/r5.anchor: الظلم في الآية مطلق وهو في إطلاقه ذو مراتب بحسب درجات الأفهام

TABRISI:6:82/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:82/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:82/r1.claim: In Arabic, ẓulm is putting something outside its proper place; poetry uses the word for improperly cutting a camel or diverting rain from its course.
TABRISI:6:82/r1.anchor: قال الأصمعي: الظلم في اللغة وضع الشيء في غير موضعه

TABRISI:6:82/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:82/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:6:82/r2.claim: “Not mixing faith with injustice” means not mixing it with shirk, as Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib, Qatāda, Mujāhid, and most exegetes hold; Ubay b. Kaʿb cites Luqmān’s declaration that shirk is grave injustice.
TABRISI:6:82/r2.anchor: والظلم هو الشرك عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن المسيب وقتادة ومجاهد وأكثر المفسرين

TABRISI:6:82/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:82/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:6:82/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the verse troubled the Companions, who asked who had not wronged himself; the Prophet clarified that the intended injustice was shirk, citing Luqmān 31:13.
TABRISI:6:82/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال:

TABRISI:6:82/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:82/r4.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:6:82/r4.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī and al-Balkhī say injustice includes every grave sin that cancels the reward of obedience, broader than shirk alone.
TABRISI:6:82/r4.anchor: وقال الجبائي والبلخي: يدخل في الظلم كل كبيرة تحبط ثواب الطاعة

TABRISI:6:82/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:82/r5.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:6:82/r5.claim: Al-Balkhī argues that restricting injustice to shirk would imply an unrepentant major sinner is secure, which conflicts with rejection of irjāʾ; the author responds that this inference does not follow from the verse’s implication and other evidence makes such a sinner insecure.
TABRISI:6:82/r5.anchor: ولو اختص الشرك على ما قالوه لوجب أن يكون مرتكب الكبيرة إذا كان مؤمنا كان آمنا

TABRISI:6:82/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:82/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:82/r6.claim: Security is reward and protection from punishment, while being guided means judged to follow truth and religion; another interpretation takes it as guidance to Paradise.
TABRISI:6:82/r6.anchor: من الله بحصول الثواب والأمان من العقاب

TABRISI:6:82/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:82/r7.speaker: علي
TABRISI:6:82/r7.claim: One view, transmitted from ʿAlī, makes the statement part of Abraham’s speech to his people.
TABRISI:6:82/r7.anchor: إنه من تمام قول إبراهيم ع وروي ذلك عن علي ع.

TABRISI:6:82/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:82/r8.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TABRISI:6:82/r8.claim: Muḥammad b. Isḥāq, Ibn Zayd, and al-Jubbāʾī instead take it as God’s judgment resolving the dispute between Abraham and his people.
TABRISI:6:82/r8.anchor: وقيل: إن هذا القول من الله تعالى على جهة فصل القضاء بذلك بين إبراهيم ع وقومه عن محمد بن إسحاق

THALABI:v4p164/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p164/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p164/r11.claim: Ibrahim asks which side deserves security; God judges that those who believe without mixing faith with shirk have security and guidance.
THALABI:v4p164/r11.anchor: فقال الله عز وجل قاضيا وحاكما بينهما الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r1.claim: The words about those who believe and do not mix faith with wrongdoing continue Abraham’s argument, as if a learned speaker asks and answers himself.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r2.claim: The words are Abraham’s people replying to his question about which group deserves security, using the verse as their answer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r2.anchor: قوم إبراهيم لإبراهيم أجابوه لما سألهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r3.claim: The words are God’s own verdict distinguishing Abraham and his adherents from the other group.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r3.anchor: هذا من قول الله تعالى على جهة فصل القضاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r4.speaker: ابن عباس؛ سعيد بن جبير؛ ابن جريج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r4.claim: Wrongdoing here means associating partners with God, or disbelief and shirk; Ibn Jurayj says no one disputed that interpretation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r5.speaker: علقمة عن ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r5.claim: When Muslims feared that any personal sin invalidated security, the Prophet explained that the verse means shirk and cited Luqmān’s description of shirk as grave wrongdoing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r5.anchor: ألم تسمعوا ما قال لقمان لابنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r6.claim: The verse proves that whoever dies without associating partners with God must ultimately be secure from the Fire.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p254/r6.anchor: من مات لا يشرك بالله وجب أن يكون عاقبته الأمن من النار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p256/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p256/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p256/r1.claim: The promised security is from punishment, and the guided are directed to God’s religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v8p256/r1.anchor: يريد: من العذاب، {وهم مهتدون} يريد: أرشدوا إلى دين الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:6:80-82/r4.claim: Believers who do not mix faith with shirk are secure from punishment and guided to God’s religion.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r1.claim: The predominant view is that Abraham himself supplies the answer to his question about which side is safer, since no other answer is possible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r1.anchor: Ağırlıklı görüşe göre bu âyetteki ifade de Hz. İbrâhim’e aittir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r2.claim: Believers who do not mix faith with injustice means Abraham's people believed in God but also associated other supposed deities with Him; injustice here means shirk, denying God's exclusive right to divinity and lordship.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r2.anchor: Âyetteki zulümden maksat, Allah’a şirk koşmaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r3.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r3.claim: The Prophet says God's right over His servants is that they worship Him and associate nothing with Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r3.anchor: Allah’ın kulları üzerindeki hakkı O’na kulluk edip hiçbir şeyi kendisine ortak koşmamaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r4.claim: A sound report says Muslims panicked, thinking they could not avoid all injustice in life; the Prophet clarified that the verse means the injustice in Luqman's warning against associating partners with God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:82/r4.anchor: Bunun üzerine Resûlullah âyete şu şekilde açıklık getirmiştir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: The reference to Abraham and later prophets asserts that they invited people to Muhammad’s same message; Muhammad must follow their guidance and leave rejecters to themselves, since he must preach but cannot force belief.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: His responsibility is to only preach and he is not liable to force people to accept guidance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: Abraham is singled out because Israelites and Ishmaelites both claimed him as patriarch and guide while attributing their inherited religious practices to him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: both the Israelites and the Ishmaelites regarded him as their patriarch and spiritual leader.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.claim: Judaism, Christianity, and Ishmaelite polytheism are later fabrications with no connection to Abraham; Muhammad’s mission revives and completes Abraham’s religion for his descendants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p58/.anchor: it was also essential to make it evident to the Ishmaelites that the religion of polytheism they have adopted is their own fabrication

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.claim: Ẓulm here means polytheism, as elsewhere in the Qur'an; acceptable faith must be entirely free of it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.anchor: in the last verse refers to polytheism. It is used in this meaning at

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.claim: True security and guidance belong to people who trust God in all affairs and clear themselves of polytheism, rather than relying on deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p68/.anchor: The fact is that peace is reserved for those who trust God in all affairs and absolve themselves of polytheism.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p213/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p213/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p213/r1.claim: Qatada explains the injustice that believers must not mix with faith as associationism.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p213/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم ﴾ قال بشرك

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p213/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p213/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p213/r2.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Muslims feared they could not meet the condition because they wronged themselves; the Prophet clarified that the verse means shirk, citing Luqman’s description of it as great injustice.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p213/r2.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليس ذاكم أما سمعتم قول لقمان لابنه ﴿ إن الشرك لظلم عظيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r7.claim: The apparent speaker of the answer is Abraham: he voices the answer to his own rhetorical question, identifying believers as the party entitled to safety.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p570/r7.anchor: الظاهر أنه من كلام إبراهيم لما استفهمهم استفهام عالم بمن هو الآمن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r1.claim: Other proposals make the answer Abraham’s people admitting an argument against themselves, or God’s words commanded to Abraham, or a divine verdict separating the disputants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r1.anchor: هو من كلام الله أمر إبراهيم أن يقوله لقومه أو قاله على جهة فصل القضاء بين خلقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r2.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r2.claim: Ali is reported to take “those who believe” as Abraham and his companions; another report attributed to him says Abraham alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r2.anchor: وليست في هذه الأمة قاله علي وعنه إبراهيم خاصة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r3.speaker: عكرمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r3.claim: Ikrima restricts the believers to those who migrated to Medina; another report takes them generally, which Abu Hayyan regards as the apparent scope.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r3.anchor: أو من هاجر إلى المدينة، قاله عكرمة أو عامة قاله بعضهم وهو الظاهر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r4.claim: Ibn Masud and Ubayy identify the ظلم that excludes safety as shirk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r4.anchor: والظلم هنا الشرك قاله ابن مسعود وأبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r5.speaker: رسول الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r5.claim: When Companions worried that everyone wrongs themselves, the Prophet explained this verse by quoting Luqman: associating partners with God is a great wrong.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r5.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r6.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r6.claim: When Umar asked what the wrong meant, Ubayy answered that it was shirk, relieving him; Zayd ibn Suhan and Salman had a similar exchange.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r6.anchor: ولما قرأها عمر عظمت عليه فسأل أبيا فقال: إنه الشرك يا أمير المؤمنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r7.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r7.claim: Mujahid's wording “with shirk” is a gloss on the meaning rather than a canonical reading, since it differs from the written consonantal text.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r7.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد: ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بشرك ولعل ذلك تفسير معنى إذ هي قراءة تخالف السواد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari interprets the wrong as a grave sin that makes a person dissolute, arguing that “mixing” fits sin but not simultaneous faith and shirk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r8.anchor: أي لم يخلطوا إيمانهم بمعصية تفسقهم وأبى تفسير الظلم بالكفر لفظ اللبس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan calls this a concealed Mu'tazili position: the Prophet explicitly interpreted the wrong as shirk, so that explanation should be accepted over al-Zamakhshari's reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r9.anchor: وهذه دفينة اعتزال أي إن الفاسق، ليس له الأمن إذا مات مصرا على الكبيرة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r10.claim: The wording permits “did not mix” to continue the relative clause or to be a circumstantial clause; Arabic permits a wāw with a negative clause, contrary to claims that it is rare or required.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r10.anchor: ولم يلبسوا يحتمل أن يكون معطوفا على الصلة ويحتمل أن يكون حالا دخلت واو الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r11.claim: Ikrima reads the verb with a ḍamma on yāʾ; the clause can have an omitted subject or predicate, while al-Nahhas and al-Hawfi's alternative parsing is remote.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p571/r11.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة: ولم يلبسوا بضم الياء ويجوز في الذين أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق وابن زيد والجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r1.claim: The explanation that true believers are secure may be God's own resumption, clarifying the correct answer to Abraham's question.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r1.anchor: من جهته تعالى مبين للجواب الحق الذي لا محيد عنه وروي ذلك عن محمد بن إسحاق وابن زيد والجبائي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r2.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r2.claim: A report from Ali says the clarification is spoken by Abraham.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r2.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون من جهة إبراهيم عليه السلام وروي ذلك عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r3.claim: The grammatical objection says this is not a resumption because it answers an actual question, whereas grammatical resumption should begin speech disconnected from what precedes; the author answers that disconnection means no syntactic attachment, not no semantic link.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r3.anchor: إن الاستئناف النحوي ما كان في ابتداء الكلام ومنقطعا عما قبله وهذا مرتبط بما قبله لارتباط الجواب والسؤال ضرورة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r4.speaker: ابن هشام
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r4.claim: Ibn Hisham defines grammatical resumption as a new opening not connected to what precedes; the author replies that this means syntactic independence, although semantic connection remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r4.anchor: لما قال ابن هشام إن الاستئناف النحوي ما كان في ابتداء الكلام ومنقطعا عما قبله

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r5.claim: The referent may identify which group deserves security: those who believe in what must be believed.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : المراد بابتداء الكلام ابتداؤه تحقيقا أو تقديرا أي الفريق الذين آنوا بما يجب الايمان به

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وابن المسيب وقتادة ومجاهد وأكثر المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r6.claim: Most commentators, including Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Musayyib, Qatada and Mujahid, interpret 'wrongdoing' as shirk; idolaters claimed worshipping others alongside God completed their faith by bringing them nearer and interceding.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#2/r6.anchor: وإلى تفسير الظلم بالشرك هنا ذهب ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وابن المسيب وقتادة ومجاهد وأكثر المفسرين

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Companions were troubled by this verse and asked who had never wronged himself; the Prophet clarified that the intended grave wrongdoing was shirk, as Luqman told his son.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r1.anchor: أخرجه الشيخان وأحمد والترمذي عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه أن اة ية لما نرلت شق ذلك على الصحابة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r2.claim: Although the hadith does not prove that other wrongdoing is not injustice, the indefinite noun is magnifying: 'great injustice' points to shirk, or the unqualified term denotes its fullest instance.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r2.anchor: لأنهم قالوا : إن التنوين في ( بظلم ) للتعظيم فكأنه قيل : لم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم عظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r3.speaker: الجبائي والبلخي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r3.claim: Al-Jubba'i and al-Balkhi, followed by al-Zamakhshari and most Mu'tazilites, interpret wrongdoing as sin rather than shirk.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r3.anchor: وقيل : المراد به المعصية وحكي ذلك عن الجبائي والبلخي وارتضاه الزمخشري تبعا لجمهور المعتزلة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r4.claim: The Mu'tazilites argue that security is exclusive to those without sin, so a grave sinner cannot be secure or escape punishment; they say 'mixing' is compatible with sins but not with shirk.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r4.anchor: واستدلوا بالآية على أن صاحب الكبيرة لا أمن له ولا نجاة من العذاب حيث دلت بتقديم لهم الآتي على اختصاص الأمن

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r5.claim: They reject the hadith as a solitary report that cannot oppose categorical proof and say shirk cannot coexist with faith because the two are opposites.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r5.anchor: والحديث خبر واحد فلا يعمل به في مقابلة الدليل القطعي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r6.claim: The claim that a sinner is neither believer nor unbeliever fails because faith is often used for assent itself, while assent may coexist with shirk, as the Qur'an says many believe in God while associating others with Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r6.anchor: بل لا يكاد يفهم منه بلفظ الفعل غير هذا حتى أنه يعطف عليه عمل الصالحات كما جاء في غير ما آية وأجيب بأنه أريد بالإيمان تصديق القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r7.claim: If faith means assent to all required beliefs, mixing need not mean simultaneous belief and shirk: unbelief may cover and overwhelm belief, or a person may alternate between faith and unbelief.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r7.anchor: بل تغطيته بالكفر وجعله مغلوبا مضمحلا أو اتصافه بالإيمان ثم الكفر ثم الإيمان ثم الكفر مرارا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r8.claim: Even if security is reserved for people without sin, that does not establish that sinners are certainly punished; it only leaves them fearful and exposed to that possibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r8.anchor: إنما يدل على اختصاص الأمن بغير العصاة وهو لا يوجب كون العصاة معذبين البتة بل خائفين ذلك موقعين للاحتمال

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r9.speaker: some exegetes
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r9.claim: Another view takes security to mean safety from eternal punishment, not freedom from any punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r9.anchor: وقيل المراد من الأمن الأمن من خلود العذاب لا الأمن من العذاب مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r10.claim: The preferred syntax makes the relative pronoun a subject, then 'those' a second subject whose predicate is 'they have security'; alternatives treat 'those' as apposition or the relative phrase as predicate of an omitted subject, which al-Alusi calls remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p207#3/r10.anchor: والموصول مبتدأ واسم الإشارة مبتدأ ثان والإشارة إلى الموصول من حيث اتصافه بما في حيز الصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p208/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p208/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p208/r1.claim: The believers are guided to truth; everyone else is in manifest error. Some specify the path that guarantees safety from eternal punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p208/r1.anchor: إلى الحق ومن عداهم في ضلال مبين وقدر بعضهم إلى طريق توجب الأمن من خلود العذاب
